input: We're putting a bounty on this labeling issue, $400 for whoever gets batch_07 in and merged. One person please, see the comments. https://github.com/openleaf/cassava-lesions/issues/142
sourceText:
Help wanted: bounding-box annotations for batch_07 (600 images) #142
Open · labels: help wanted, data, bounty
opened by nkemdirim-o

We have 600 field photos in data/raw/batch_07/ (collected in Ogun and Oyo states, October 2024) that have no annotations yet. This batch is the last one blocking the v0.4 training run.

Classes — use exactly these label strings:
- cmd (cassava mosaic disease)
- cbsd (cassava brown streak disease)
- cbb (cassava bacterial blight)
- cgm (cassava green mite damage)
- healthy_leaf

Guidelines:
- One box per visible leaf that shows symptoms, plus healthy_leaf boxes for up to 3 clearly healthy leaves per image.
- Boxes tight to the leaf edge, include the petiole only if it shows lesions.
- Skip leaves smaller than 32px on the short side.
- If an image is too blurred or shows no cassava, do not annotate it; add the filename to data/annotations/batch_07_skipped.txt with a one-word reason (blur, not_cassava, duplicate).
- Full guideline with example images: docs/ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md.

Tooling: CVAT (project template in tools/cvat_labels.json) or Label Studio. Export as COCO 1.0.

Deliverable: a single PR adding data/annotations/batch_07.json and batch_07_skipped.txt. CI runs `make validate-annotations`, which checks the COCO schema, category ids against categories.yaml, and that every image in batch_07 is either annotated or listed as skipped.

Quality gate: 40 gold images are hidden inside the batch. Before merging we compute mean IoU and class agreement on those. We need mIoU >= 0.75 and class agreement >= 90%. If it falls short we'll leave review comments and you can fix and push again.

Comments

farida-k: Can I split this with a friend? 300 each?
nkemdirim-o: Prefer one PR from one person so the gold check is clean and we don't get inconsistent box styles.

tobi-dev: is cgm the green mite one? the guide only has 2 examples
nkemdirim-o: Yes, cassava green mite. Look for fine yellow stippling and leaves that look shrunken or 'candlestick' at the shoot tip. Added 6 more examples to the guide.

adaeze-n: Is it ok to use a pretrained model to pre-label and then correct?
nkemdirim-o: Fine, as long as every box is reviewed by hand. The gold check will catch lazy pre-labels.

input:
Project: Data entry — 2024 Cook County assessment notices into our appeal-prep spreadsheet

Who we are
Halvorsen Diaz is a six-person property tax appeal firm in Chicago. Every reassessment year we get a wave of scanned assessment notices from clients and need them in a spreadsheet before our analysts can pull comparables. This is Batch B of the north-side townships.

What you get
- A shared Google Drive folder "2024_Notices_Batch_B" with 340 PDFs. Most are scans of the 2-page paper notice from the Assessor's office; some are phone photos converted to PDF (crooked, some glare). File names are our internal client IDs, e.g. HD-24-0417.pdf.
- A subfolder "Priority" with 61 of those PDFs (Lake View and Rogers Park townships, whose appeal windows close first).
- A template Google Sheet "Batch_B_Entry" with headers and data validation already set up, plus a "Reference" tab with 5 rows we filled in ourselves as worked examples.

Fields (one row per PIN, NOT per PDF — roughly 30 notices list two or more PINs, each gets its own row with the same client_id)
1. client_id — from the file name
2. pin — 14-digit Property Index Number, formatted XX-XX-XXX-XXX-XXXX
3. property_address — exactly as printed, including unit numbers
4. township — as printed
5. property_class — 3-digit code without the dash (2-11 becomes 211)
6. prior_year_av — prior year assessed value, integer, no $ or commas
7. current_av — current year assessed value, integer
8. current_market_value — integer
9. building_sqft — if printed, blank otherwise
10. land_sqft — if printed, blank otherwise
11. notice_date — YYYY-MM-DD
12. appeal_deadline — YYYY-MM-DD (the 'last day to file' line on page 1)
13. entry_notes — anything odd: handwriting on the notice, a second page missing, a PIN that doesn't match the address

Rules
- Do not guess. If a value is unreadable, enter UNREADABLE and say in entry_notes which page and field.
- OCR is fine to speed things up, but every number must be checked by eye against the PDF. We have been burned by OCR turning 8s into 3s.
- Confidentiality: these notices carry client names and home addresses. Work in the browser from the shared Drive. Do not upload the PDFs to any third-party OCR or AI service outside Google Workspace, and delete any local copies when done. We will ask you to confirm this in writing at handoff.

Timeline
- Priority subfolder (61 PDFs) entered within 2 business days of getting access.
- Full batch within 6 business days of getting access.

Acceptance criteria
- All 340 client_ids appear in the sheet, plus extra rows for multi-PIN notices. Our check column on the Reference tab flags any missing file.
- Every PIN passes the validation column (cell turns green).
- We pull a random 30-row sample and check every field against the PDF. At least 98% of sampled fields must match exactly, and there must be zero errors in the pin and appeal_deadline columns in the sample.
- No UNREADABLE cell without a note explaining page and field.
If the sample fails, you get one revision pass over the full sheet and we re-sample.

Pay
$600 flat for the whole batch, one person. Questions to dana@halvorsendiaz.com before you start, not halfway through.

Kestrel Swap: Dune dashboard brief

Context
We're Kestrel, a concentrated-liquidity DEX on Arbitrum One, live since March. Team of 6, no data person. Our investors and the Arbitrum grants committee keep asking for public numbers, and right now we screenshot our internal Postgres, which nobody trusts. We want a public Dune dashboard that becomes the canonical source.

Contracts (Arbitrum One)
- Factory: 0x7b1E...c4A2 (deployed at block 187,442,019)
- Router v2: 0x3f9a...91De
- Fee collector: 0x55c0...0b17
Our contracts are already decoded on Dune under kestrel_arbitrum (Factory_evt_PoolCreated, Pool_evt_Swap, Pool_evt_Mint, Pool_evt_Burn, Pool_evt_Collect). If anything is missing, submit a decoding request. Don't hardcode topic hashes.

What we need on the dashboard
1. Daily and cumulative volume in USD across all pools, with a 7d moving average.
2. TVL by pool (top 15) and total, daily. Use prices.usd / prices.day. For tokens with no Dune price, fall back to the pool-implied price against USDC or WETH and flag it.
3. Fee revenue: LP fees vs protocol fees, daily and monthly.
4. Unique traders per day and per week. Count tx_from (the EOA), NOT the swap event sender, which is our router.
5. Top 20 pools table: TVL, 7d volume, 7d fees, fee tier, volume/TVL.
6. LP retention: of wallets that minted a position in a given week, the % still holding a position 4 and 8 weeks later.
7. A 'last updated' counter and a text widget explaining the methodology.

Technical requirements
- DuneSQL only. No legacy Spark.
- Every query must run in under 60 seconds on the free-tier engine, or be split into a materialized view.
- Parameterize pool address and date range where it makes sense.
- Queries must be clean enough that we can fork them, with comments on any non-obvious join.

Acceptance criteria
- Dashboard is public under our team handle 'kestrel' (we'll add you to the team), not your personal account.
- For 1 Aug to 31 Aug, total volume, total fees and unique traders are within 2% of the CSV export we'll share from our indexer.
- No double counting of multi-hop swaps routed through two pools. Per-hop is fine for 'pool volume', but the headline number must be per-trade. Explain which you did.
- Wash-trading flag: pools where one address is >50% of 7d volume are highlighted, not excluded.

Budget and timing
$1,500 flat, one person. We'd like it within 2 weeks of starting. Ping @mara_kestrel on Telegram with questions.

persona: Rafael Duarte, grants manager at the Halyard Foundation, which funds the ecosystem around Halyard Markets, an isolated-market lending protocol on Base
input:
Halyard Ecosystem Grant: open-source liquidation keeper

About us
Halyard Markets is an isolated-market lending protocol on Base, live on mainnet since January. Today liquidations depend on two professional searchers. When gas spiked during the April selloff, three positions sat underwater for 40+ minutes and the protocol took bad debt. We want a reference keeper that anyone can run, so liquidation coverage never depends on a couple of private bots again.

Scope
An open-source (MIT) liquidation bot in TypeScript or Rust that:
- Discovers all markets from HalyardFactory (0x91c2...e3F0) via MarketCreated events. No hardcoded market list.
- Tracks borrower health using on-chain reads plus event indexing, and recomputes on every oracle update (both our Chainlink and Pyth adapters are used).
- Calls liquidate(market, borrower, repayAmount) when the health factor is < 1, sized to the 50% close factor.
- Supports flash-loan funded liquidation through Morpho Blue or the Balancer vault, so operators need no inventory.
- Includes a profitability check covering gas plus the L1 data fee on Base, with a configurable minimum profit.
- Uses the public mempool by default, with optional private submission via a builder RPC.
- Ships as a Docker image with a one-command run and Prometheus metrics.

Milestones
M1: Design + fork simulation (30% of grant). A design doc, plus a Foundry/Anvil fork test replaying the April 14 window (Base blocks 13,402,100 to 13,404,900) showing the bot would have liquidated the three positions. Deliverable: public repo, doc, CI green.
M2: Testnet (30%). Bot running against our Base Sepolia deployment for 14 consecutive days. We will create at least 10 unhealthy positions, and the bot must liquidate at least 9 of them within 3 blocks of becoming liquidatable. Deliverable: keeper address plus the list of liquidation tx hashes.
M3: Mainnet release (40%). A v1.0.0 tagged release with docs, a light review of any helper contract by a reviewer we name, and the bot run on Base mainnet by the grantee for 30 days. It must execute at least one real liquidation, or show it missed none by comparison against our indexer.

Grant size: $9,000 total in USDC, paid per milestone. One grantee (an individual or a small team).

Out of scope: a front end, MEV backrunning strategies, other chains.

How to apply: reply with your GitHub handle, bots or keepers you've shipped before, your language choice, and a time estimate for M1.

M1 fork replay of Base blocks 13,402,100 to 13,404,900 liquidating the three April positions
M2 at least 9 of 10 liquidations on Base Sepolia within 3 blocks over 14 days, proven by keeper address and tx hashes
M3 v1.0.0 MIT release plus 30 days on Base mainnet, checked against Halyard's indexer

PRODUCT PHOTOGRAPHY BRIEF - Shitalakshya Weavers Collective

1. Who we are
We are a collective of 35 jamdani weaving households in Rupganj, Narayanganj. Most of our sarees are sold through middlemen at the Demra haat. This year we want to sell directly, first to a boutique buyer in Gulshan who has asked for a look book, and later through our own Facebook shop. We have no product photos except some phone pictures taken in bad light.

2. What we need
Professional-looking product photographs of 60 jamdani sarees. The sarees will be ready, ironed and tagged with an SKU (SWC-001 to SWC-060) in our community hall in Tarabo. The photographer must come to the hall. We cannot send the sarees to Dhaka.

3. Shots per saree (3 shots each, 180 images total)
 a) Full drape on a plain mannequin or hanging from a rod so the whole length and pattern are visible
 b) Pallu (anchal) detail, flat, showing the motif clearly
 c) Border close-up, flat, with the weave texture visible
No human models. No props, flowers or jewellery.

4. Technical requirements
- Plain white or very light grey background for all shots
- Natural daylight or daylight-balanced lights. Colours must match the real fabric. Our buyer has complained before that red came out orange in photos.
- Minimum 2000 x 2000 pixels, JPG, sRGB
- Lightly edited only: crop, straighten, exposure, white balance. No changing the colour of the saree, no removing weaving irregularities (those show it is handmade)
- File names: SKU_shot letter, for example SWC-014_a.jpg, SWC-014_b.jpg, SWC-014_c.jpg
- Also one group photo of the weavers in front of a loom, only for those who agree. Ask each person, we will make a list of who has agreed

5. Delivery
- Upload all files to a Google Drive folder we will share, in one folder per SKU
- Add a simple sheet listing SKU, file names and any saree that had a problem (stain, missing, could not be photographed)
- Shoot day: any Friday or Saturday this month, between 10am and 3pm when the hall has best light. Delivery of edited files within 7 days of the shoot

6. Acceptance criteria
- 180 product images present, correctly named, in the correct SKU folders
- All on white/light grey background, sharp, no visible clutter
- Rukhsana and two senior weavers will compare 10 random sarees side by side with the photos on a laptop; colours must look true
- Group photo includes only people on the consent list
- If more than 10 images fail, the photographer re-shoots those sarees at no extra cost

7. Payment
BDT 20,000 (around USD 180) total for one photographer, including travel from Dhaka and editing. Paid after acceptance. We prefer a woman photographer because many of our weavers are more comfortable, but this is not required.

8. Contact
Rukhsana Begum, coordinator. Phone or WhatsApp available after the photographer is selected. Please speak Bangla, most weavers do not speak English.

Status: Approved by Grants Committee (4 of 5 votes)
Author: 0xmarisol

Summary
QuillSwap v3 launched without a maintained subgraph. Integrators, aggregators and our own frontend currently rely on a fork of the v2 subgraph that misses concentrated-liquidity positions entirely. I propose building and maintaining a v3 subgraph and a lightweight public analytics dashboard.

About me
I have shipped subgraphs for two lending protocols and contributed to graph-tooling. GitHub: github.com/0xmarisol

Milestones
M1: Testnet subgraph. Index all v3 pools on Arbitrum Sepolia. Entities: Pool, Token, Swap, Mint, Burn, Position, Tick, plus PoolDayData and PoolHourData aggregates. Deployed to Subgraph Studio with a public query endpoint and the schema documented in the repo.
M2: Mainnet subgraph. Published to The Graph decentralized network on Arbitrum One, fully synced to chain head. For the top 20 pools by TVL, reported reserves must match on-chain reserves within 0.1% at a block the committee picks.
M3: Dashboard and docs. Open-source Next.js dashboard (pools, volume, fees, top positions) live at a public URL, reading only from the subgraph. README covering local setup, schema and example queries for integrators.

Timeline: roughly 10 weeks total.
Maintenance: I commit to fixing indexing breakages for 6 months after M2.

Comments
kaito (committee): Approved. Please add a FeeTier entity so integrators can filter by 0.05 / 0.3 / 1% tiers. Payment per milestone after committee review.
lena.eth (committee): +1. For M2, post the deployment ID and the block you verified against.
0xmarisol: Will add FeeTier in M1. Thanks all.

Northgate Builder Fund - Grant Agreement Summary (Cohort 3)

Recipient: Kofi Mensah (solo developer, github.com/kofimensah)
Project: Tipjar - passkey-based tipping for independent podcasters on Base
Total grant: $20,000 USDC, paid in four tranches

Context
We fund small consumer apps on Base that onboard people who have never held a wallet. Kofi's Tipjar lets a listener tip a podcaster from a link in the show notes using a passkey (Face ID / fingerprint) instead of a seed phrase. The smart account is created on first tip; gas is sponsored by a paymaster Kofi runs. The podcaster gets a dashboard with tips received and can withdraw to any address.

We pay by milestone, not by time. Each tranche is released after we review the evidence listed below. If a milestone is going to slip more than 3 weeks past its target, email grants@northgate.fund before the date, not after.

Milestone 1 - Prototype ($4,000, target: week 4)
- Smart account factory and tipping contract deployed to Base Sepolia.
- Web flow: open a tip link, create a passkey, tip in test USDC, see confirmation.
- Public repo with a README explaining how to run it locally.
Acceptance: contract addresses on Base Sepolia with verified source on Basescan; tx hash of a completed test tip; repo link.

Milestone 2 - Demo ($4,000, target: week 8)
- Podcaster dashboard: list of tips, totals, withdraw.
- Paymaster sponsoring gas for the first 3 tips per new account.
- 3-5 minute unedited screen recording of a new user on a phone going from tip link to confirmed tip in under 60 seconds, then the podcaster withdrawing.
Acceptance: video link; a staging URL we can try ourselves.

Milestone 3 - Mainnet deploy ($6,000, target: week 12)
- Contracts deployed to Base mainnet, source verified.
- Independent review: a short audit from a firm, or a public review by two reviewers we approve. Any high-severity findings fixed before deploy.
- Production URL live.
Acceptance: mainnet contract addresses; review report; at least one real tip tx on mainnet.

Milestone 4 - Users ($6,000, target: week 20)
- 250 unique smart accounts created through Tipjar, each having sent at least one tip on Base mainnet.
- Tips spread across at least 10 different podcasters.
- Measured over a window of at least 14 days.
- Sybil filter: no more than 10% of accounts may be funded from the same source address. Accounts created by Kofi or by participating podcasters don't count.
Acceptance: a Dune query or CSV of account addresses and tip tx hashes we can spot-check on Basescan.

Out of scope
- No token. No points program. Do not pay users to tip.
- Native iOS/Android apps not required; mobile web is fine.

Reporting
Short written update at each milestone (what shipped, what broke, what's next), posted in #cohort-3.

Questions go to Hana Sato, programme manager.

Research Scope: Cross-Domain MEV between Osmosis and Neutron
Prepared by Halyard Labs Research. v1.2, agreed with Dr. Adaeze Okafor

Background
Osmosis and Neutron are connected over IBC and share many of the same assets. Our relayer logs show frequent price gaps between Osmosis pools and Astroport pools on Neutron that close within a few blocks, which suggests active cross-domain arbitrage. Nobody has measured how much of this happens or who captures it.

Research questions
1. How much cross-domain arbitrage occurs between Osmosis and Neutron, by month, over the study window?
2. Which actors (addresses, relayers) capture it, and how concentrated is it?
3. Does IBC relayer latency explain missed opportunities?

Study window: 1 October to 31 December 2024.

Milestones
M1: Literature review and methodology (target: week 3). An 8-12 page document covering prior work on cross-domain MEV (Ethereum L2s and Cosmos), detection heuristics, and data sources (archive nodes, Numia, Mintscan). Must state the exact Osmosis and Neutron block height ranges covering the study window.
M2: Dataset (target: week 7). Public Google Sheet or CSV listing every detected arbitrage pair: both tx hashes, chain, block height, timestamp, assets, estimated profit in USD at block time, and a detection confidence score. Scripts in a public repo so Halyard can reproduce a random 50-row sample.
M3: Final report and talk (target: week 12). 25-40 page report answering the three questions, with charts. A 30-minute recorded talk at the Halyard community call, slides shared.

Independence
Findings are Dr. Okafor's. Halyard may comment on drafts but will not edit conclusions. The report is published under CC BY 4.0.

Comments
Adaeze Okafor: Agreed. I will need archive node access for Neutron. Can Halyard provide an RPC endpoint?
Marcus Lindqvist: Yes, I will share credentials for our archive node by week 1.

mustCarry: recipient Dr. Adaeze Okafor (invite-only)
study window 1 Oct to 31 Dec 2024, Osmosis and Neutron
M1: 8-12 page methodology with exact block ranges
M2: public sheet/CSV of arbitrage pairs plus scripts reproducible on a 50-row sample
M3: 25-40 page CC BY 4.0 report plus a 30-minute recorded talk at the April community call

Accepting the M2 dataset without the public scripts needed to reproduce the sample

Research: compare DA options for Driftwood mainnet (Ethereum blobs vs Celestia vs EigenDA vs Avail) #412
Open · labels: research, help wanted
opened by @mkovacs

Context
We currently post batches to Ethereum as EIP-4844 blobs. Over the last 30 days we averaged ~40 tx/s at peak hours and roughly 2.1 MB/hour of compressed batch data. Blob fees have been fine most days, but this quarter we had three spikes where posting costs jumped about 20x for several hours. Before we commit to anything, we want a written comparison we can point governance at.

What we need
A markdown doc at docs/research/da-comparison.md covering:
1. Cost per MB for each option, with the methodology: which fee data, which date range, how you converted. Show it at our current volume and at 5x.
2. Latency and finality: time until data is considered available, and until our derivation pipeline can safely use it.
3. Trust assumptions: what we are trusting in each case (DAS light nodes, restaked operators, committee, etc.) and what happens if the DA layer withholds data.
4. Integration with OP Stack alt-DA mode: what exists today (da-server implementations), the maintenance burden, and which options are production-used by other OP chains.
5. Failure modes and fallback: can we fall back to Ethereum blobs automatically?

Put a summary table at the top and cite sources inline (docs, explorers, dashboards). Don't use vendor marketing as the primary source for numbers.

Out of scope
Implementation. A recommendation is welcome, but label it clearly as opinion.

Comments
@jdlr: Can we include Ethereum calldata as a baseline too? Even if it's obviously worse, governance will ask.
@mkovacs: Yes, add calldata as a baseline row.
@aseno: For EigenDA please note whether we'd need to pay for reserved bandwidth vs on-demand. That changes the math a lot at our volume.
@mkovacs: Good point, add it. Also: one PR, keep it under ~3,000 words, tables count separately.

persona: Anand Kulkarni, CEO of Kirana Cold, an 11-person Pune startup running electric refrigerated last-mile delivery for dairy and pharma
input:
Market sizing brief: Kirana Cold (Pune)

Who we are
Kirana Cold runs electric refrigerated three-wheelers and small vans for last-mile delivery of dairy, frozen foods and temperature-sensitive pharma in Pune and Nashik. We're 11 people and our seed round closes in Q3. We need a defensible market size for the deck and for our own expansion planning. Investors keep poking holes in the top-down numbers we lifted from a consulting report.

What we want
A bottom-up TAM / SAM / SOM for refrigerated last-mile delivery in Indian tier-2 cities. By last mile we mean the last 30 km, from distributor or C&F agent to retailer, pharmacy, cloud kitchen or hospital. Size it for FY2025, with a 5-year projection to FY2030.

Scope
- Segments: (a) dairy & frozen (ice cream, paneer, frozen snacks); (b) pharma cold chain at 2-8°C (vaccines, insulin, biologics) to pharmacies and hospitals. Exclude fruits & veg, and exclude meat/seafood for now.
- Geography: SAM covers these 12 cities only: Nashik, Aurangabad, Nagpur, Indore, Bhopal, Surat, Vadodara, Coimbatore, Madurai, Mysuru, Lucknow, Jaipur. TAM covers all tier-2 cities. Use either the RBI or the Census Tier II classification and say which one you used.
- SOM: what we could realistically capture by FY2028 given our fleet plan (40 vehicles now, target 250 by FY2028).

Method requirements
- Bottom-up: number of delivery points (retail outlets stocking frozen, chemists, hospitals) x drops per day x revenue per drop. Cross-check against a top-down number, and explain the gap if it is over 30%.
- Every assumption in its own cell, with a source or a clearly labelled estimate. Sources we trust: NHB / NCCD cold chain studies, CDSCO and state drug controller licence counts, Census 2011 + MoSPI, company filings (Amul, Hatsun, Mankind etc.), FSSAI licence data. You may cite paywalled reports only if you quote the figure and the page.
- Show figures in INR crore and USD million, and state the exchange rate used.
- A sensitivity table for the 3 assumptions that move the number most.

Stages and payment (total $1,800, paid per stage on acceptance)
1. Methodology note (2 pages max) + source list + the delivery-point datasets you plan to use. $400. Due 7 days after start.
2. Google Sheet model: an inputs tab, calc tabs per segment and per city, an outputs tab, and the sensitivity table. Formulas live, no pasted values in the calc tabs. $700. Due day 18.
3. Final memo (4-6 pages) + 8-10 slides we can drop into the deck, with charts from the sheet. $700. Due day 25.

Acceptance criteria
- I (Anand) and our ops lead review each stage and reply within 3 working days.
- Every number on the slides traces back to a cell in the sheet.
- Every source has a working link or a page reference.
- No made-up sources. We will spot-check 10 citations, and if any of them don't exist the stage is rejected.
- City-level numbers for all 12 cities, not just totals.

Nice to have
A short note on which 3 of the 12 cities we should enter first, and why.

What we'll provide
Our current drop data from Pune (anonymised, ~6 months), our unit economics per drop, and the fleet plan. You sign an NDA before you get the drop data.

mustCarry: Three stages: methodology note ($400, day 7), live-formula Google Sheet model ($700, day 18), memo + 8-10 slides ($700, day 25)
The 12 named tier-2 SAM cities, with city-level numbers for each
Segments limited to dairy/frozen and 2-8°C pharma; fruits/veg and meat/seafood excluded

Figures in INR crore and USD million with the exchange rate stated

[RFP] Governance tooling comparison: moving Orchard DAO to onchain voting
Category: Grants > RFPs · posted by orchard-steward-lena

Summary
Orchard DAO currently votes on Snapshot, with a 3-of-5 multisig executing results on Optimism. The Season 6 mandate from token holders asks us to evaluate moving to binding onchain voting. Before a binding proposal, the Grants Council wants an independent comparison of the main options.

Tools in scope
- Snapshot with oSnap (UMA optimistic execution)
- Tally (OZ Governor)
- Agora
- Aragon OSx

Evaluation criteria
1. Cost per vote for a delegate on Optimism, and the total cost of a typical proposal lifecycle (propose, vote, queue, execute). Use real transactions where possible.
2. Delegation UX: how easily a token holder with no crypto experience can delegate, redelegate, and see what their delegate did.
3. Safety: timelock support, veto or Security Council patterns, guardian roles, upgrade paths.
4. Migration effort from our current setup: contracts, token (our ORCH token is not ERC20Votes today), frontend, docs.
5. Vendor lock-in, and what happens if the frontend provider shuts down.
6. Accessibility and mobile support.

Milestones
Milestone 1 (week 2): evaluation framework, criteria weights, and notes from interviews with at least 3 active delegates (we'll introduce you). Posted as a reply in this thread.
Milestone 2 (week 6): final report posted as a new forum topic, with a comparison table, scored results, a clear recommendation, and a migration outline for the recommended option.

Requirements
- Disclose any past or current relationship with any of the four vendors. Undisclosed conflicts void the grant.
- All gas and cost figures must link to transactions or a reproducible method.
- Report licensed CC BY 4.0.

How to apply
Reply with a short background, links to past research, and any conflicts. The Council will pick one researcher within 10 days.

Replies

orchard-steward-lena: Added to criterion 4, thanks.

Backend developers at small SaaS companies, comfortable with REST, probably never used Ledgerline, may be reading on a second monitor while coding. Assume Node or Python. Do not assume they know GST invoicing rules; link to our /concepts/tax page instead of explaining.

Brief: LinkedIn posts for Gareth (CEO), June

Who we are
Quarrystone is a 14-person company in Leeds. We make procurement software for mid-size UK construction contractors: firms turning over £10m to £80m that still run purchase orders off spreadsheets, email and the site manager's WhatsApp. Our buyers are commercial directors, quantity surveyors and site buyers. Nearly all of them are on LinkedIn. Almost none are on X, so this is LinkedIn only.

What we need
Four LinkedIn posts written for our CEO, Gareth Okafor, to publish from his personal profile, one a week starting Tuesday 3 June. Gareth posts them himself. You are writing, not posting, and you won't need his login.

The four posts
1. The materials price shock. Gareth was a QS for 11 years before Quarrystone. In 2022 a job he was on lost most of its margin because steel rebar quotes were three weeks stale by the time the PO went out. Tell that story honestly and land on why quote freshness matters.
2. 'The WhatsApp PO'. Why site teams order through WhatsApp, why that's rational for them, and what it costs the commercial team at month end. Don't sneer at site managers. They are our users.
3. Retentions. A short, opinionated post on how late retention release hurts subcontractors, and what main contractors can do about it with better records. This one can be spikier.
4. Supplier Scorecard launch. Our new feature goes live 24 June. It ranks suppliers on delivery accuracy, price variance against quote and credit-note frequency. Name the feature once, and only once. This is not an advert, it's Gareth explaining why we built it.

Requirements
- Each post 180 to 300 words.
- UK English (organisation, programme, labour).
- The hook has to land in the first two lines. LinkedIn truncates at roughly 210 characters on mobile.
- End with one real question or a clear next step. Not 'Thoughts?' and not 'Agree?'
- Max 3 hashtags per post, at the end, never mid-sentence.
- No emoji bullet lists, no 'In today's fast-paced world', no 'Here's the thing:', no one-line-per-paragraph broetry for the whole post.
- No invented statistics. Any number must come from the source pack or from a public source you link in a doc comment (ONS, BCIS, CITB and the like are fine).
- Do not name customers. Bramwell & Sons can be referred to as 'a Yorkshire groundworks firm' and nothing more specific.
- Don't mention competitors by name.

What you'll get
- A 20-minute call with Gareth (he talks fast, record it).
- A Google Drive source pack: three of his old conference talks, anonymised customer interview notes, and the Supplier Scorecard one-pager.
- Two of his past posts that did well and one he hated, so you can hear his voice.

Deliverable
One Google Doc shared with comment access to marketing@quarrystone.co.uk. For each post include: the post text, the word count, a suggested first comment (Gareth likes to drop the link there rather than in the post), and a one-line note on the image or visual if one helps.

Deadline and acceptance
- All four drafts in the doc by Friday 30 May, 17:00 BST.
- Every post inside the word range, and none of the banned phrases above.
- One round of revisions is included. Gareth signs off. We accept when he says it sounds like him, not like a content agency.
- Payment is not tied to likes, reach or comments. We know LinkedIn is a lottery.

Budget: $600 for all four posts, one writer. Construction or B2B SaaS writing experience is a big plus, so please link something you've written.

'xero vs myob' and 'best accounting software for sole traders australia' are our two highest-intent keywords and we currently rank nowhere for either. Audience
Sole traders in their first 1-3 years, usually doing their own books at night, often switching from spreadsheets or a shoebox of receipts. Not accountants. Many will read this on their phone.

4. 'Which should you choose' section by scenario (just got an ABN; registered for GST; hiring a first apprentice; working with a bookkeeper).

- All six structure items present.
- Every competitor claim has a dated source.
- Australian English throughout.
- Meta title and description within character limits.
- Our head of product signs off on Ledgerly feature accuracy (we'll do this in comments within 3 business days).

Timeline and pay

Owner: Dmitri | Status: Hiring operator

Goal: Maximize our allocation in the Merid L2 points program before the snapshot (rumored end of September). Merid has said allocation is weighted by unique wallets, active days, and bridged volume, and that they run sybil filtering on clustered wallets. We need to look like 300 independent users.

- Generate 300 fresh EVM wallets, each in its own browser profile (AdsPower or Dolphin Anty), each with its own residential proxy.

Phase 2 — Activity (week 3-8)
- Each wallet bridges to Merid via the official bridge at least once, then makes 2-4 interactions per week across MeridSwap, Lendro, and the NFT mint contract.

Phase 3 — Maintenance & claim (until claim window)
- Keep activity going until snapshot. After claim opens, claim from each wallet and consolidate via different CEX deposit addresses over 2 weeks so the consolidation isn't visible on-chain.

Reporting
- Weekly sheet with wallet address, active days, bridged volume, Galxe points.
- Flag any wallet that appears on public sybil lists (e.g. if Merid publishes a sybil report) so we can retire it.

Opened by mareike-k (maintainer)

In scope
- https://staging-api.ledgerloop.dev (all /v2 endpoints)

- Third-party services (Stripe, Postmark, Google)
- Rate-limit findings without demonstrated impact

Chairside — Research brief: Front-desk rescheduling pain (Q3)

Context
Chairside is an 11-person team in Toronto. We sell scheduling + recall software to independent dental clinics (1-4 chairs) in Ontario and BC. Churn in months 2-4 sits at 9% and nearly every exit survey blames 'too many clicks to rebook'. Honestly, we don't know what the front desk does during a reschedule, and our PMs keep guessing. Who we want to talk to
- Front-desk staff / office managers at independent clinics (NOT DSO-owned chains)
- At least 2 current Chairside customers
- At least 3 using Dentrix, ABELDent or Tracker
- Max 1 person per clinic
- 6 interviews total, 45-60 min, on Zoom, recorded with consent

Marguerite

Accessibility audit: Kweli Pay web onboarding (WCAG 2.2 AA)

Hi, I'm Achieng, Head of Product at Kweli Pay. We're a 22-person team in Nairobi building a mobile-money-linked wallet. Our web onboarding (sign up > phone verification > KYC with national ID > set PIN > link M-Pesa) launches to the public on 2 December, and our bank partner requires a documented accessibility review before go-live. We have never done one properly. Looking for ONE experienced auditor.

SCOPE
- Environment: https://staging.kwelipay.co.ke/onboarding (basic auth creds + 3 test phone numbers shared privately after you accept)
- Screens in scope (7): Welcome, Phone number, OTP entry, ID type selection, ID upload (front/back + selfie), Create PIN, Link M-Pesa
- Out of scope: logged-in dashboard, marketing site, the native Android app
- Standard: WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Pay special attention to 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (our OTP and PIN screens), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured.
- Assistive tech: NVDA + Firefox on Windows, VoiceOver + Safari on iOS, TalkBack + Chrome on Android. Keyboard-only on desktop. 200% zoom and 320px reflow.
- Languages: the flow ships in English and Kiswahili. Check that lang attributes switch and that screen readers pronounce Kiswahili correctly.

STAGE 1: AUDIT (due 8 November)
Deliver a Google Sheet, one row per issue, columns: ID, screen, WCAG criterion number, severity (blocker / major / minor), assistive tech + browser + OS, steps to reproduce, expected, actual, screenshot or short clip link, suggested fix. Plus a one-page summary doc: what passes, the top 5 blockers, anything you couldn't test and why.

STAGE 2: RETEST (within 5 working days of us telling you fixes are on staging, expected around 22 November)
Retest every blocker and major from Stage 1, mark each row Fixed / Partially fixed / Not fixed with a fresh screenshot, and add any regressions you find. Short sign-off note we can forward to the bank.

BUDGET
$1,800 total: $1,200 when Stage 1 is accepted, $600 when Stage 2 is accepted.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- All 7 screens covered with all three screen readers and keyboard-only
- Each issue maps to a specific WCAG 2.2 success criterion. No generic "improve contrast" rows without the measured ratio.
- Each issue is reproducible by our devs from the steps alone
- No automated-scanner dumps. axe/Lighthouse output is fine as a supplement, not as the audit.
- Test data only. Never enter a real ID number or a real M-Pesa number.
- Findings are confidential until launch. Don't post screenshots publicly.

Nice to have: experience with East African fintech or with Kiswahili screen-reader output. Please tell us which AT versions you used.

Tidepool v2 rewrites our lending pools with isolated markets and a new liquidation engine. Before audit #2 we want real humans clicking through the whole lifecycle on Base Sepolia and telling us what's broken or confusing.

1. Get Base Sepolia ETH from any public faucet.

Help wanted: clear the Q&A backlog in GitHub Discussions #1187
opened by mkessler-dev · labels: help wanted, community

We have 41 threads in the Q&A category of Discussions with no accepted answer, some going back to March. Most are about the same handful of things: retry/backoff config, running workers under Kubernetes with graceful shutdown, the Postgres backend vs the Redis backend, and migrating from 0.9 to 0.11 (the JobContext rename).

The core team (three of us, all part-time) can't keep up, and unanswered questions are the number one complaint in the community survey.

What we're looking for
- One person who knows tidewater reasonably well (you've used it in production or contributed).
- Answer up to 25 of the open Q&A threads. Pick any, oldest first preferred.
- Each answer should include a working code snippet against v0.11.x where relevant, and link to the relevant docs page or source line.
- If the question is actually a bug, don't guess: reproduce it if you can, open an issue linking the discussion, then reply in the thread with the issue link. That counts as an answer.
- Don't answer threads where a maintainer already replied in the last 30 days.

What counts
An answer counts once a maintainer marks it as the answer, or the original poster replies confirming it solved their problem. We'll do a pass twice a week.

Deadline: end of October.

When you're done, comment on this issue with a list of the discussion links you answered.

3) Remove the early-return that skips fee collection.
4) Add Foundry tests: (a) normal release splits correctly, (b) a malicious seller contract that re-enters release() must not drain funds, (c) release reverts if called twice.

- `forge test` passes including the three new tests.
- No funds can be released twice.
- Fee math: feeAmount = amount * feeBps / 10000, seller gets amount - feeAmount.
- Gas: don't regress release() by more than ~5k gas vs current.

Project: Series A deck redesign, Brightwater Health

About us
Brightwater Health is a 22-person company in Leeds building remote monitoring software for post-surgical patients. We're raising a GBP 8M Series A starting the week of 17 March. Our current deck (18 slides, Google Slides) was built by the founders in a hurry and it shows: inconsistent fonts, screenshots pasted at random sizes, three different greens. The story and the numbers are final and have been reviewed by our lead investor's associate. We need the design to catch up.

What we need
A full visual redesign of the existing 18-slide deck. Not a rewrite. You will get:
- The current deck (Google Slides link)
- Our brand guidelines PDF (logo, primary navy #0B3D5C, accent teal #1FA39A, typeface Inter)
- 6 product screenshots at full resolution
- Raw data for the 4 charts (Google Sheet)

Deliverables
1. Redesigned deck in Figma (16:9, 1920x1080 frames), one frame per slide, built from components for title, body, chart and footer so we can edit later.
2. PDF export, under 15 MB, fonts embedded.
3. A Google Slides version of slides 1, 2, 17 and 18 only (we present these live and edit them per meeting).
4. The 4 charts rebuilt as vectors from the raw data, not traced from the old screenshots.

Requirements
- Keep every number, claim and the slide order exactly as they are. If you think a slide should change, leave a comment in Figma; don't change it.
- Max 40 words of body text per slide. If a slide is over, flag it and we'll cut.
- Product screenshots placed in device frames (laptop for the clinician dashboard, phone for the patient app).
- WCAG AA contrast for all text.
- No stock photos of doctors shaking hands. We mean it.
- Appendix slides (15 to 18) can be simpler but must use the same system.

Timeline
- Day 3: style direction, 3 sample slides (cover, traction chart, team) for sign-off.
- Day 8: full draft.
- Day 10 (Friday 7 March): final files.
One round of feedback after the style direction, one after the full draft.

Acceptance criteria
- All 18 slides present, in original order, at 1920x1080.
- Every figure matches the source deck and the sheet exactly (we will check each one).
- Figma file shared with edit access to design@brightwaterhealth.co.uk, with a components page.
- PDF under 15 MB, opens correctly in Preview and Acrobat.
- The 4 Google Slides versions open without missing fonts.
- Our CEO and CFO sign off.

Budget is $1,800 fixed for the whole thing, paid on final sign-off. One designer. Please include 2 or 3 deck or presentation samples when you apply.

Homepage hero illustration: brief
Owner: Dara Okafor (Comms). Status: Open for illustrators. Last edited 3 Feb

Context
Saltmarsh Collective restores coastal wetlands along the Essex and Suffolk coast with local volunteers. We're relaunching saltmarsh.org.uk in April and the homepage currently uses a drone photo that loads slowly and says nothing about the people involved. We want one illustration that does the job of that photo and more.

What it should show
- A tidal saltmarsh at low tide: creeks, mudflats, sea lavender, a few wading birds (redshank or curlew, not flamingos, this has happened before)
- 3 to 5 volunteers of different ages doing real restoration work: planting, building brushwood fences, carrying monitoring equipment
- A hint of the sea wall and a distant village on the left edge
- Calm, hopeful. A bit of humour is welcome.

Style
Flat-ish vector with some texture, limited palette. References in the gallery below (Tom Haugomat, Malika Favre's landscape work, the Wildlife Trusts 2023 annual report). Nothing photoreal, no 3D.
Palette: mud #6B5B4B, marsh green #5E7F5A, sea lavender #9C8CC4, sky #E8EEF2, accent #E07A3F. Tints are fine.

Technical
- 2400 x 1200 px artboard, with the right third kept quiet enough to place a headline over it on desktop
- A mobile version at 1080 x 1350 that still reads (can be a separately adjusted artboard)
- Deliver: layered SVG, AI or Figma source, PNG and WebP exports at 1x and 2x
- No text inside the illustration
- SVG under 400 KB after optimisation

Rights
Full copyright assignment to Saltmarsh Collective. You may show it in your portfolio.

Timeline
Rough sketch by 14 Feb, final by 28 Feb. One round of revisions on the sketch, one on the colour version.

Gallery: 6 reference images
